answer: A library I am very fond of is the public library in Sirajganj, a modest but well-kept building not far from the town centre. It is not grand, but it has a [[quiet dignity]] about it, with rows of tall wooden shelves and long reading tables. I try to go a couple of times a month, usually on a free afternoon when I need to study or simply want some quiet. The moment you step inside, you are enveloped in a wonderfully [[hushed]] atmosphere that immediately calms the mind. It has a decent collection of Bengali literature as well as some English books, so I can always find something interesting to read. I usually borrow novels, but I also read the daily newspapers there and occasionally look through books on business and management. What I love most is the sense of [[reverence]] people seem to have there; everyone respects the silence, which is increasingly rare. I usually sit at the same desk in a quiet corner near the back, which is my favourite spot. There is something deeply [[gratifying]] about being surrounded by so many books and knowing I will never run out of things to discover. Many students from less well-off families also rely on it for exam preparation, which makes it even more valuable to the town. Honestly, in an age of screens and constant noise, a library feels almost like a [[sanctuary]]. I think these places are precious, and I hope they never disappear.

followUps.q: Do you think libraries will still exist in the future?
followUps.answer: I think so, but they will need to change. They will probably offer more digital resources and study spaces, but people will always need quiet places where they can read and think.

followUps.q: Do you prefer printed books or e-books?
followUps.answer: Printed books, without doubt. I read on my phone when I am travelling, but I love the feel of a real book, and I remember what I read much better on paper.

note: 'Central library in my city' made the public library in Sirajganj, described modestly (no invented grandeur or huge collection); added what he reads and its value to students; plain 'satisfying' mark replaced by 'gratifying', added 'quiet dignity'.
